title: Write the headline after the verdict
statement: Compose a feedback headline only after the verdict exists, from the same writer, because praise written before the verdict can congratulate a wrong answer above its own correction.
example: In one build's vocabulary say-back, wrong answers were congratulated above their correction until a single writer composed both; a new gate holds it at 19 of 19.
detail: In a Grade 3 reading build's vocabulary say-back, a child who gave a wrong answer was congratulated, 'Nice! That word is now yours', with the correction printed underneath. The cause was ordering: the congratulation was written before the verdict existed, so it could not have agreed with it. The panel now has a single writer, so the headline cannot contradict the judgement below it, and a new gate holds the fix at 19/19, measured on the build on 2026-07-30.

evidence.quote: a child who gave a *wrong* answer was being congratulated
written before the verdict existed, so it could not possibly have agreed with it.
